Container.Name: Supermemory
Container.Overview: One memory store on your own server for your coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes and anything else that speaks the Supermemory API can save what they learn to it and recall it later.
Container.Description:
Runs Supermemory's self-hosted server (supermemory-server, the "lite" build). It serves the Supermemory memory API and hybrid search on one port and keeps its database, embedding model and API key in the App Data path.
The server binary is not in the image. The first start downloads the release named by Server Version from Supermemory's GitHub releases into App Data (about 300 MB) and checks its SHA-256; later starts reuse it.
Set one LLM provider before the first start: an OpenAI key, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LLM Base URL plus a key and a model), an Anthropic key or a Gemini key. The server uses it to extract memories from what clients send. After the container is healthy, read the API key from store/api-key in App Data and give it to your clients. Set Console Password to open the server's web console from the WebUI button.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: memory agent Claude Code Codex OpenCode OpenClaw Hermes RAG vector search AI assistant context
Container.Requires: Unofficial template; not affiliated with Supermemory. The container needs internet access on its first start to download the server and the embedding model. An LLM provider is required. The server's own license notice limits this build to 10,000 documents. It has no connectors and no MCP endpoint. The App Data path holds every stored memory and the API key; treat it as a secret and back it up. Keep the port on a trusted LAN or a VPN such as Tailscale; do not expose it to the internet. Support: https://github.com/ntindle/unraid-apps/issues

Config.Name: API Port
Config.Description: Host TCP port mapped to container port 6767. Clients use http://[IP]:[PORT] as their Supermemory base URL.

Config.Name: Console Port
Config.Description: Host TCP port mapped to container port 6769: the server's web console, behind Console Password. Answers only when Console Password is set.

Config.Name: Console Password
Config.Description: Password for the web console (user admin). Anyone who signs in can read and change every stored memory. Leave empty to keep the console off.

Config.Name: App Data
Config.Description: Persistent state: the downloaded server (bin), the database, embedding model and API key (store). Contains every stored memory; include it in backups.

Config.Name: LLM API Key
Config.Description: Key for OpenAI, or for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint in LLM Base URL. Leave empty if you set an Anthropic or Gemini key instead.

Config.Name: LLM Base URL
Config.Description: Leave empty for OpenAI. For an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (a proxy, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter) enter its /v1 address. The endpoint must serve /chat/completions with tool calls.

Config.Name: LLM Model
Config.Description: Model the OpenAI or OpenAI-compatible provider runs. Leave empty for the server's default OpenAI model; required for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Config.Name: Anthropic API Key
Config.Description: Use Anthropic as the LLM provider instead.

Config.Name: Gemini API Key
Config.Description: Use Gemini as the LLM provider. Also the only key that lets the server read images, video and scanned PDFs.

Config.Name: Server Version
Config.Description: supermemory-server release to run. Changing it downloads that release on the next start. Back up App Data first: an older server may not read a newer database.

Config.Name: Host Guard
Config.Description: On: every API request needs the API key. Off: the server's own behaviour, where a request that sends a loopback Host header skips the key; only for a port no other machine can reach.

Config.Name: User ID
Config.Description: User the server runs as and that owns App Data.

Config.Name: Group ID
Config.Description: Group the server runs as and that owns App Data.
